J U D G E M E N T

[
1
]

The Court hereby confirms and gives the reasons for a decision
rendered verbally at the hearing of October 7
th
, 2002, in accordance
with the requirements of section 90 of the law.

[
2
]

The Court was presented with two petitions by the Director of Youth
Protection to have the security and development of J... and L... B... declared
compromised because the parent’s behaviour or way of life creates a risk of
moral or physical danger for the children.

[
3
]

Furthermore, in the case of J..., the Director of Youth Protection
invokes section 38 h) to the effect that the child has serious behavioural
problems and the parents do not or cannot take the steps required to resolve
them.

[
4
]

The principal allegations in support of the Director's petitions
are  the following:

•

On June 19
th,

2001, the mother was awarded interim custody by the Superior Court, a copy of
the judgment is filed herein as Exhibit R-2;

•

The father has a
history of verbally and physically abusive behaviour towards the mother and the
children;

•

The father has been
charged with assault on J... as well as his wife and is awaiting trial;

Concerning J...:

•

The child is physically
aggressive toward his mother;

•

The child has expressed
suicidal ideations;

•

The child has
threatened his mother with a knife and has hit his mother with a broom;

•

The child has admitted
to difficulty in controlling his anger.

[
5
]

The Director of Youth Protection recommends that the children be
entrusted to their mother with aid, counsel and assistance and that the
contacts with the father be supervised.

[
6
]

The mother admits to the majority of the allegations of the
petitions and agrees with the measures proposed by the Director of Youth
Protection.  She testifies that the children were witness to some of the
arguments that they have had over the years.  She states that the father was
violent towards her; he pushed her, put holes in the wall and swore.  He was
rough  with the children and during one incident hurt his son's hand. The
mother adds that J..., is making efforts to control his temper, his behaviour
is much less violent.

[
7
]

The father admits the majority of the allegations and is in
agreement with most of the recommendations made by the Director. He admits that
there have been conflicts between himself and the mother and that they both
have charges of assault and harassment pending.  The children have been witness
to some of these outbursts. The father maintains that the mother has also
demonstrated anger and inappropriate behaviour during these incidents. He
wishes to have unsupervised visits with his children and explains that it is
difficult to find a third party to supervise, especially for a whole day.  He
has not seen the children recently and wants to resume contacts as soon as
possible. He states that he does not feel the need to participate in an anger
management program or therapy.

[
8
]

The Court also heard the testimony of Ms. Linda Murphy, Youth
Protection Delegate, and read the reports the Director of Youth Protection
filed as proof of the children's situation.  It is clear from the evidence
presented to the Court that the parents have a conflictual relationship that
has lead to violent outbursts, to which the children have been witness.
Unfortunately, and it was apparent at the hearing, their remains a lot of
tension and anger between the parents. This has an impact on the children and
their behaviour.    Therefore,  both parents should follow a therapy,  if not
to resolve their own

[
9
]

personal issues, at least to learn how to help their children cope
with their difficulties and the separation.  As parents, Ms. U... and Mr. B...
have to put the needs of their children before their own.

[
10
]

The evidence and the admission made have
convinced the Court that the security and development of the children are
compromised.

[
11
]

THEREFORE, THE COURT :

[
12
]

GRANTS the petition;

[
13
]

DECLARES compromised the security and development
of the children, J... and L... B...;

[
14
]

ORDERS that the children be entrusted to their
mother, Ms. U…

[
15
]

ORDERS that the frequency and modality of
contacts between the father and the children be determined by the Director of
Youth Protection under the following conditions: that the visits be supervised
until December 31
st
, 2002;

[
16
]

ORDERS that both J... and L… continue to be seen
by psychiatric nurse, Ms. Luscia Fabijian, at the Jewish General Hospital, for
as long as deemed necessary;

[
17
]

ORDERS that both children be psychiatrically
assessed at the Jewish General Hospital or in a private clinic;

[
18
]

RECOMMENDS that Ms. U...follow a therapy to
address personal issues;

[
19
]

RECOMMENDS that Mr. B... follow a therapy to
address personal issues;

[
20
]

ORDERS that aid, counsel and assistance be
provided to the family and the children for a period of one year.

[
21
]

ENTRUSTS the situation of the children, J... and
L... B..., to the Director of Youth Protection of Batshaw Youth and Family
Centres, who shall see that the measures are carried out;

[
22
]

ORDERS the execution of the present judgement by
any peace officer.

Ann-Marie Jones, J.C.Q.
